incompatibleNotice.contradictionNote: The list says the extension is there and the object says it is not. That is not a weaker disguise — it is a self-contradiction, and it costs a detector two calls with no permission, no timing and no reference device. Anti-fraud systems check exactly this pair, because it is the cheapest way to catch a rewritten extension list.
incompatibleNotice.reportsListNote: The browser reports the profile's extension list, but it cannot make an extension work. So a page reads this:
incompatibleNotice.warningModalTitle: This fingerprint does not fit this machine
incompatibleNotice.webgpuNote: These behave differently from the extensions above: the browser does not claim them. It reports the profile's list narrowed to what this machine really has, so nothing contradicts itself — the adapter just reports a shorter list than the device the profile names would.

inlineEditor.androidMediaHelp: Almost every Android device is Widevine L1, so a real phone accepts hardware-secured playback and this one refuses it — which a site can read in one call. Turning this on makes the profile answer like the device it claims to be. The catch: this browser reaches Widevine through a software module, so a site that believes the answer and asks for a hardware-secured licence gets one it cannot play. Leave it off where paid video has to work; turn it on where matching the device matters more.
inlineEditor.androidMediaLabel: Answer DRM questions the Android way
inlineEditor.cookiesHelp: A JSON array, the shape the browser's own export writes. Loaded once the profile is saved.
inlineEditor.refreshRateHelp: A page reads this by timing how often the browser draws. Frames can only be slowed down, so a rate above this computer's own screen quietly runs at the screen's. 60 is what most machines report.
inlineEditor.resolutionHelp: Only what this monitor can show — {w} × {h}. A larger claim is contradicted by the window itself.

settings.apiHelp1: Local HTTP API (axum) for scripting — create/launch/close profiles and get a CDP WebSocket URL. Binds
settings.apiHelp2: only, JWT Bearer auth. Changes to enable/port apply after restarting the app.
settings.cameraHelp1: The profile gets ShardX's camera instead of the machine's, and shows the picture or clip you pick from the control left of the browser's app menu.
settings.cameraHelp2: The profile's fingerprint already names a particular camera, so handing a page the host's real one contradicts the profile and identifies the machine behind every profile on it.
settings.extraArgsHelp1: Appended to every profile launch, one per line or space-separated. They go on
settings.extraArgsHelp2: , so a switch repeated here is the one the engine sees — which is also how you get to undo one of the launcher's own. Quote a value with spaces.
settings.extraArgsHelp3: Anything that changes what a page can measure belongs in the profile, not here: a switch applied to every profile at once makes them all alike, which is the opposite of what a profile is for.
settings.geoCheckerHelp1: Which free public IP-geo service to hit when you press the proxy
settings.geoCheckerHelp2: button. All three are no-key, rate-limited.
settings.helperHelp1: Watches each page for fields a generated identity fits — names, email, phone, date of birth — and offers to fill them. It only ever
settings.helperHelp2: : nothing is typed until you press the button on the panel that appears. Values come from the profile's own language, and go in through the same human typing the rest of the browser uses.
settings.helperHelp3: In a group whatever you type in one window is mirrored into the others already, so a helper per window would find the same form ten times and offer ten prompts for one page.
settings.helperNeverSync: Never runs on a synchronised launch.
settings.helperTriggersHelp: Nothing selected means every kind. Narrow it if the panel appears on forms you do not care about — a login page with an email field is still a form.
settings.languageHelp: The launcher's own text. The browser's language comes from the profile.
settings.loadErrorBody1: What you see below are the defaults — your file was left untouched, and saving here keeps a copy of it as
settings.mcpDownloadDialogTitle: Where to download the MCP server
settings.mcpHelp2: server source (lets an AI client drive profiles and a CDP browser) into a folder you choose. The app does not run it — install its deps and register it with your MCP client per the included README. Requires Node.js.
settings.screenHelp1: reports the screen carried in the bound profile (recommended for anti-detect coherence).
settings.screenHelp2: lets ShardX expose the host monitor's actual size.
